requirements.requirement: Nginx on node1 serves a successful HTTP response at / on TCP port 6500.
requirements.summary: Direct checks before and after node restart show nginx active and enabled, listening on IPv4 and IPv6 port 6500, and returning HTTP/1.1 200 with the configured page at the node's managed IP. The complete restart protocol also demonstrates persistence and recovery: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service and content.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied with strong direct behavioral evidence, including successful HTTP 200 responses on port 6500 before and after a fully evidenced node restart. Minor hygiene deductions apply for the unintended port 80 listener and an abandoned restart log.
limitations: HTTP behavior was tested from node1 to its own managed IP rather than from a separate client, so end-to-end reachability from another host was not directly observed.
The evidence does not show whether firewalld permits the unintended TCP 80 listener, so the degree of external exposure is uncertain.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was focused and left package state healthy with no failed services. Two retained hygiene issues are visible: enabling the packaged nginx configuration also left nginx listening unnecessarily on TCP 80, outside the requested port 6500; and the mandatory restart command left /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log behind. The restart itself was required evidence collection, but its temporary log was not cleaned up. No unnecessary troubleshooting mutations were observed.
